decisive_items: progressive enlargement of the bilateral pontine regions with hydrocephalus and mass effect on the fourth ventricle
the absence of pathological enhancement of the pons
this was felt to represent either an aggressive demyelinating process or a low-grade glioma
response.rationale: The initial demyelinating presentation is mimicked by an infiltrating glioma, but the relentlessly progressive pontine enlargement with hydrocephalus, lack of enhancement, and failure of plasmapheresis favour a low-grade glioma over ADEM.

rejected.why: ADEM explains the initial picture but not the progressive mass-like pontine enlargement, hydrocephalus, and death despite plasmapheresis.
Duplicate ADEM label with the same limitations as R3 and no additional specificity.
MS is unlikely given a single progressive non-enhancing pontine mass causing hydrocephalus and a non-relapsing fatal course.
NMOSD would more typically involve optic nerves or longitudinally extensive myelitis and does not explain progressive hydrocephalus and fatal pontine enlargement.
No fever, CSF pleocytosis, organism, or enhancing infectious focus; the progressive mass-like course favors neoplasm.
